intent: compare current sports betting research apps
title: The 8 Best Sports Betting Research Apps in 2026, Compared
seoTitle: 8 Best Sports Betting Research Apps in 2026
description: We compared eight sports betting research apps by the work they do best, from AI agents and historical systems to line shopping, prop research, and bet tracking.
dek: One app finds a better number. Another explains a prop. Another remembers whether your picks actually won. We compared eight of them, including the one we built, around the work they are genuinely good at.
author: chris-habib

disclosure: We make WagerProof, and we publish this guide. We are not going to pretend that makes us neutral. Our top pick applies to bettors who want agents, historical Systems, transparent records, Discord, and outside AI connections in one place. Every competitor still gets a genuine win where it is better suited to the job.
verdict: If you want one research home instead of a stack of disconnected tools, start with WagerProof. Its agents work the slate, Systems test ideas against history, every published pick gets graded, and the same research can follow you into Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP clients. OddsJam still wins for large-scale line shopping, Props.Cash for quick visual prop work, Pikkit for automatic sportsbook tracking, and Rithmm for no-code model building.

apps.name: WagerProof
apps.categoryLabel: Best overall for AI agents, Systems, and transparent records
apps.price: Free limited tier; Pro pricing appears in-app and varies by region
apps.summary: WagerProof puts a configurable team of AI agents beside its own models, live sportsbook lines, historical Systems, WagerBot, player-prop tools, Discord community, and AI integrations. Every published pick and saved System keeps getting graded, so the record does not stop when the screenshot looks good.
apps.whyItWins: It keeps the whole research loop in one clean product. You can find a model and market disagreement, let agents research it, test the idea against history, inspect the public record, and bring the same data into Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or another compatible AI through the WagerProof MCP connector.
apps.limitation: Choose a specialist if your only goal is broad arbitrage scanning or automatic sportsbook syncing. WagerProof's current historical Systems cover MLB, NFL, and college football, while models cover five sports and cross-book props cover MLB and NFL. The free plan includes one active AI agent. Pro raises that to 30 total agents, with up to 10 active, and adds Historical Systems, cross-book props, unlimited WagerBot, and Discord access.

apps.name: Juice
apps.price: Official March 2026 page: $6.99 weekly or $99.99 yearly after a 3-day trial; verify checkout
apps.summary: Juice starts with the thing already on your phone: a bet-slip screenshot. Upload it and the app compares live prices while showing probability and expected-value estimates from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok.
apps.whyItWins: Its official workflow is direct: upload the slip, review the live price, and compare four named AI estimates side by side. It is built for the bettor who wants a quick second opinion on something already sitting in the bet slip.
apps.limitation: It is a screenshot-first research tool, not a historical System builder or a public performance ledger. Its public pages do not include an independent accuracy audit, and the App Store purchase labels make checkout the safest place to confirm the billing period.

apps.name: OddsJam
apps.categoryLabel: Best for market scanning and line shopping
apps.price: Modular plans; current U.S. App Store tiers range from $19.99 monthly to $399.99 monthly
apps.summary: OddsJam is the power tool in this list. It scans a large sportsbook set for line shopping, positive-EV spots, arbitrage, middles, promotional conversions, player trends, and tracking.
apps.whyItWins: Nothing else here is as focused on finding price differences across a huge number of books. If your research starts with the market and you are willing to operate a more demanding setup, OddsJam is the clearest choice.
apps.limitation: The product is priced in modules rather than one simple all-access plan. Its own plan selector also makes clear that the advanced workflows can require several sportsbook accounts, a meaningful bankroll, and hours of daily attention.

apps.name: Outlier
apps.categoryLabel: Best blend of prop context and price tools
apps.price: Premium $19.99 monthly; Premium+ $29.99 monthly; Pro $79.99 monthly
apps.summary: Outlier sits between a visual prop app and a serious price tool. It combines player and game context, injuries, line movement, alerts, odds comparison, and higher-tier EV or arbitrage screens.
apps.whyItWins: It is built for bettors who want to understand the player and shop the price without switching products. Its official feature set puts contextual stats, injuries, line movement, and price comparison in the same workflow.
apps.limitation: The Android app is not yet the same product as the web and iOS versions. Outlier says Android currently supports Premium and MLB, while several Premium+ and Pro features remain elsewhere.

apps.name: Props.Cash
apps.price: $19.99 monthly or $199.99 yearly for all sports
apps.summary: Props.Cash keeps player-prop research focused. Trend cards, filters, current lines, roster and injury context, odds analysis, and correlated-prop views are all built around answering one narrow question quickly.
apps.whyItWins: The narrow focus is the advantage. It is designed for someone who wants to open an app, understand a player's recent context, and compare a prop without first setting up a broad analytics workflow.
apps.limitation: That same focus is also the boundary. Props.Cash is not trying to be a broad game-model platform, a custom AI-agent desk, a historical System builder, or an arbitrage scanner.

apps.name: Pikkit
apps.categoryLabel: Best for verified tracking and social records
apps.price: Core tracking free; Pro $29.99 monthly or $199.99 yearly in the U.S. App Store
apps.platforms: iPhone, Android; web access is Pro
apps.summary: Pikkit is a tracker before it is anything else. BookSync pulls supported sportsbook history into profit and loss, ROI, live results, line shopping, and a social feed without asking you to grade each wager yourself.
apps.whyItWins: For an automatic record of bets you actually placed, Pikkit has the clearest workflow in this group. The verified history and social layer make it easy to follow real activity rather than manually posted wins.
apps.limitation: Pikkit does not allow manual bet entry. If your sportsbook is unsupported, you cannot simply add the wager yourself. Closing-line analysis, same-game parlay shopping, exports, alerts, and web access also require Pro.

apps.name: Action Network
apps.categoryLabel: Best for editorial breadth with odds and tracking
apps.price: Free basic product; PRO $14.99 weekly, $24.99 monthly, or $119.99 yearly
apps.summary: Action Network is the familiar all-purpose sports desk in this comparison. It puts live odds, movement, scores, tracking, expert picks, written analysis, public betting data, and alerts in one large editorial product.
apps.whyItWins: Choose it when you want to read about the game as much as you want to study the number. No other app here has the same breadth of editorial coverage tied to odds and tracking.
apps.limitation: A lot of the useful data, projections, premium articles, expert picks, and alerts sit behind PRO. It is also not built around configurable AI agents, saved historical Systems, or your own no-code model.

apps.name: Rithmm
apps.price: Core $29.99 monthly; Pro $49.99 monthly; Premium $99.99 monthly; annual plans available
apps.summary: Rithmm is for the bettor who wants to shape the model itself. You can start with a house model, build your own without code, copy a community model, shop lines, track bets, and ask Scout about the reasoning.
apps.whyItWins: It has the clearest no-code model-building path in this list. WagerProof gives you configurable agents and historical Systems, while Rithmm gives you more direct ownership over the model recipe.
apps.limitation: The feature ladder gets expensive. Scout is missing from Core and limited by monthly usage on higher plans, while advanced factors, player-impact adjustments, and exports require Premium.

faqs.question: What is the best sports betting research app?
faqs.answer: WagerProof is our best overall pick because it combines configurable AI agents, historical Systems, model and market comparison, transparent graded records, a polished interface, Pro Discord access, and MCP connections to outside AI tools. We make WagerProof, so that recommendation has an obvious conflict. OddsJam is still better for large-scale market scanning, Props.Cash for quick visual prop research, Pikkit for automatic sportsbook tracking, and Rithmm for no-code model building.

faqs.question: What makes WagerProof different from other sports betting research apps?
faqs.answer: WagerProof connects the parts that usually live in separate products. Its AI agents research and publish picks, its historical Systems test saved angles over time, and both keep visible graded records. Pro members also get Discord access, while the WagerProof MCP connector lets compatible AI clients use model, market, sports database, agent, pick, and record tools available to the signed-in account.

faqs.question: Can I use WagerProof with Claude, ChatGPT, or my own AI setup?
faqs.answer: Yes. WagerProof has a secure remote MCP connector with setup guides for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes, and it can work with other compatible clients. After you sign in and approve access, your AI can call the WagerProof tools your account is allowed to read. The connector cannot place bets, move money, or edit your data.

faqs.question: Can I build and track my own betting System in WagerProof?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the sports currently supported by Historical Analysis. Build an angle from the available filters, save it as a System, and WagerProof grades it nightly so the win-loss record, units, ROI, recent results, and streak keep changing with new games. Public Systems can also appear on the community leaderboard.

faqs.question: Can a research app guarantee profitable bets?
faqs.answer: No. A research app can organize data, estimate a probability, compare a price, test a historical idea, or keep a record. It cannot remove uncertainty. Every wager can lose, and a strong past record does not promise the next pick will win.
